questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving binary trees and traversals.
questions.stem: A written exercise: 3 - A complete binary tree has height 3. What is the maximum number of nodes it can contain?

options.misconception: it counts only the deepest level
it omits the final subtraction of one
it adds one instead of subtracting

questions.explanation: A complete binary tree of height 3 has all levels filled, giving 2 to the power (3+1) minus 1 nodes, namely 15. Choice B is a distractor: it counts only the deepest level. Choice C is a distractor: it omits the final subtraction of one. Choice D is a distractor: it adds one instead of subtracting.
questions.hint: Sum the geometric series of level sizes.

questions.stem: In a check-in problem, 5 - A complete binary tree has height 5. What is the maximum number of nodes it can contain?

options.misconception: it counts only the deepest level
it omits the final subtraction of one
it adds one instead of subtracting

questions.explanation: A complete binary tree of height 5 has all levels filled, giving 2 to the power (5+1) minus 1 nodes, namely 63. Choice B is a distractor: it counts only the deepest level. Choice C is a distractor: it omits the final subtraction of one. Choice D is a distractor: it adds one instead of subtracting.
questions.hint: Sum the geometric series of level sizes.

questions.stem: A sample problem: 14 - A binary tree has 14 internal (non-leaf) nodes. How many external null leaves does it have?

options.misconception: it assumes equal numbers of internal and external nodes

it subtracts instead of adding one

questions.explanation: In any binary tree the number of external leaves exceeds the number of internal nodes by one, so 14 internal nodes give 15 external leaves. Choice B is a distractor: it assumes equal numbers of internal and external nodes. Choice C is a distractor: it doubles the internal count. Choice D is a distractor: it subtracts instead of adding one.
questions.hint: External leaves are internal nodes plus one.

questions.stem: For a group activity, 8 - How many different labeled trees can be drawn on 8 vertices?
questions.explanation: Cayley's formula states that the number of labeled trees on 8 vertices is n to the power (8 minus 2), giving 262144. The required result is 262144.
questions.hint: Use Cayley's formula for labeled trees.
